A deterministic production-browser regression delivers that next key in the first mutation microtask after Info removal: the old dialog lifecycle leaves `BODY` focused and pause remains open. - Shared `Dialog` focus setup and restoration now use the [React layout-effect phase](https://react.dev/reference/react/useLayoutEffect), transferring focus before the next browser paint. The regression observes focus on the returned pause dialog and resumes the game with the same key. This repairs the browser focus adaptation; original artwork, animation clocks and simulation rules retain their separate fidelity boundaries.
- Verification: the new production-browser test fails on the unchanged master dialog with the same remaining-pause symptom as hosted CI, then passes with the focus change. TypeScript, formatting, all 390 rule/parser tests (5217 assertions), the production build and all 36 selected mock/synthetic/native-Info browser cases pass. The original Info/P assertion is unchanged. Reproduction logs stay ignored under `reference-captures/ci-pause-repro/`; this focus fix is landed independently of mounted-charge artwork.

### Browser verification under slow frame delivery

- Edit/help browser journeys now hold movement until the production minimap reports the east field and then the starting field, instead of guessing travel from 2900/2500 ms sleeps. Editing must still become enabled after arrival. The Info test retains its 0.05 px portrait-registration threshold with a longer convergence deadline. Production per-frame motion and the stage's existing 100 ms elapsed cap are unchanged.
- The Main-effects fixture can create a fresh flash pair and unmount the production viewport in one event. Its browser check first lets the previous pair expire, then requires an actual rendered flash sample without a game canvas before checking complete fade-out and pixel composition. This prevents historical samples or a stale pre-transition alpha-zero report from satisfying the wrong part of the journey.
- An optional test-only `BT3_E2E_FRAME_DELAY_MS` fixture delays game RAF delivery while retaining real input, timers, timestamps and cancellation. With 250 ms delays, the old travel and portrait checks failed at their original assertions; all four corrected mock edit/Info/help flows pass, including the immediate-focus regression. Expiring the old flash pair also reproduced its exact hosted assertion failure; the corrected flash transition passes the same slow-frame probe. These checks cover reconstruction and test timing, not synchronized original-runtime or complete game parity.
